title: Checks of the 2020 SST step leave 94% of the worst relative feedback range when event errors can differ
abstract: We test whether checks of one SST input change can constrain the radiative effect of several changes. Published regional tests use one error scale for all six DOISST steps in a region. We allow separate scales for each event and region, between 0.5 and 1. We keep each event global mean fixed at a scale of 0.75. With regional scale error at most 0.05, checks of all nine regions at the July 2020 change leave up to 93.9% of the initial feedback range across two periods, two correction maps and five model responses plus their mean. The common-scale test leaves 20%. Checks of all three tropical sectors at both 2005 and 2020 leave at most 59.6%. An exact search of 64 date sets selects 2005 first, then 2020. Separate linear programs and weighted-median dual calculations check the bounds. These are conditional design requirements, not measured errors or confidence limits. No new SST observation, true correction or observed feedback is inferred.

display.caption: Largest remaining relative feedback range across two correction maps and six response targets, by period. Regional scale error is at most 0.05. Separate event errors limit what checks at one input change can establish.
